source.reason: Constituent phases (austenite + ferrite) for annealed strips, κ-carbide suppression in Cr-containing strips, DO3 ordering appearing in annealed strips, ferrite fraction/morphology and reduced dislocation density for the 6Cr strip.

overall_structure.value: Two-phase austenite (γ) + ferrite (δ) microstructure; austenite is the major matrix phase and δ-ferrite is uniformly dispersed as block-like particles. After annealing at 550 °C for 5 h the constituent phases remain austenite and ferrite, and the size and fraction of ferrite almost remain the same as the as-cast strip.

source.reason: γ/δ interface and phase-interface dislocation blocking; slip band measurements for annealed 6Cr after tensile fracture; phase evolution on annealing for the 6Cr strip.

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: Increase of δ-ferrite fraction in Cr-containing strips can block dislocation propagation due to more phase-interface areas, which may decrease plasticity.

slip_behavior.value: Slip bands observed in austenite during deformation of the strips. After tensile fracture, the annealed 6Cr strip shows the finest, densest slip band set: average slip-band spacing ~60 nm and average slip-band width 7.9 nm. Smaller and less κ-carbides (relatively easy to cut through) allow multi-directional shearing, leading to narrow slip band spacing; annealing widens spacing in 0Cr (90→190 nm) but narrows it in 6Cr (80→60 nm).

phase_evolution.value: Annealing at 550 °C for 5 h leaves austenite + ferrite unchanged; promotes κ-carbide precipitation but suppressed in Cr-containing strips (superlattice still very weak in 6Cr); DO3 ordering appears in ferrite of all annealed strips including 6Cr; dislocation density in austenite reduced compared with as-cast 6Cr but still higher than annealed 0Cr.

unmapped_findings: Measured (ICP) composition of the 6Cr strip (Table 1): Fe Bal., Mn 29.1, Al 9.9, C 1.2, Cr 6.8 wt.% (Cr close to the nominal 6 wt.% target).
Measured average density of the 6Cr strip is 6.46 g/cm^3 (density analyzer SJ-600G).

The total elongation of the annealed 6Cr strip (44.3 ± 3 %) is better than that of the annealed Cr-free (0Cr) strip; the 6Cr curve extends furthest in Fig. 8(a) engineering stress-strain (close to the 50 % gridline).

The strain hardening rate of the annealed strips is higher with increasing Cr content; the reduction in strain hardening rate of annealed 3Cr strip is the largest, about 500 MPa (no numeric value given specifically for annealed 6Cr).

Slip-band data for the annealed 6Cr strip after tensile fracture: average spacing ~60 nm and average width 7.9 nm; these accompany the highest ductility except for as-cast 6Cr (dynamic slip band refinement, DSBR).
As-cast 6Cr average steady-stage strain hardening rate is reported as 2266 MPa (as-cast state; corresponds to the parent as-cast sample, not the annealed condition of this sample).
